sanskrit: na kevalaṃ śrāddhadharme puṇyakeṣv api dīyate etad vistarato rājañ śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ
english: Not only in the rite of the śrāddha, but in works of merit as well, is this given. I wish to hear of it in full and in truth, O king.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śṛṇu rājann avahitaś chatropānahavistaram yathaitat prathitaṃ loke yena caitat pravartitam
english: Bhīṣma said: Listen attentively, O king, to the full account of the parasol and the sandals—how this became renowned in the world, and by whom it was first set in motion.

sanskrit: yathā cākṣayyatāṃ prāptaṃ puṇyatāṃ ca yathā gatam sarvam etad aśeṣeṇa pravakṣyāmi janādhipa
english: And how it attained imperishability, and how it came to be accounted meritorious—all of this, without remainder, I shall declare to you, O lord of men.

sanskrit: itihāsaṃ purāvṛttam imaṃ śṛṇu narādhipa jamadagneś ca saṃvādaṃ sūryasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: Hear this ancient tale of what came to pass of old, O ruler of men—the colloquy of Jamadagni with the great-souled Sūrya.

sanskrit: purā sa bhagavān sākṣād dhanuṣākrīḍata prabho saṃdhāya saṃdhāya śarāṃś cikṣepa kila bhārgavaḥ
english: In olden days that blessed one in person sported with his bow, O lord; nocking arrow after arrow, the scion of Bhṛgu, it is said, loosed them forth.

sanskrit: tān kṣiptān reṇukā sarvāṃs tasyeṣūn dīptatejasaḥ ānāyya sā tadā tasmai prādād asakṛd acyuta
english: All those arrows of his, blazing with splendor, that he had loosed, Reṇukā fetched and brought back, and gave them to him again and again, O unfailing one.

sanskrit: atha tena sa śabdena jyātalasya śarasya ca prahṛṣṭaḥ saṃpracikṣepa sā ca pratyājahāra tān
english: Then, delighted by the sound of the bowstring against the wrist-guard and of the arrow, he kept loosing them, and she kept bringing them back.

sanskrit: tato madhyāhnam ārūḍhe jyeṣṭhāmūle divākare sa sāyakān dvijo viddhvā reṇukām idam abravīt
english: Then, when the sun had climbed to noon at the foot of the constellation Jyeṣṭhā, that brāhmaṇa, having loosed his shafts, said this to Reṇukā:

sanskrit: gacchānaya viśālākṣi śarān etān dhanuścyutān yāvad etān punaḥ subhru kṣipāmīti janādhipa
english: "Go, O wide-eyed one, fetch these arrows fallen from the bow, that I may loose them once again, O fair-browed one"—so he spoke, O lord of men.

sanskrit: sā gacchaty antarā chāyāṃ vṛkṣam āśritya bhāminī tasthau tasyā hi saṃtaptaṃ śiraḥ pādau tathaiva ca
english: As that lovely woman went, she took refuge midway in the shade of a tree and halted, for her head was scorched, and her feet likewise.

sanskrit: sthitā sā tu muhūrtaṃ vai bhartuḥ śāpabhayāc chubhā yayāv ānayituṃ bhūyaḥ sāyakān asitekṣaṇā pratyājagāma ca śarāṃs tān ādāya yaśasvinī
english: Having paused but a moment, the fair one, in dread of her husband's curse, the dark-eyed lady set out once more to fetch the arrows, and the illustrious woman returned, taking up those shafts.

sanskrit: sā prasvinnā sucārvaṅgī padbhyāṃ duḥkhaṃ niyacchatī upājagāma bhartāraṃ bhayād bhartuḥ pravepatī
english: Drenched in sweat, that fair-limbed one, bearing the pain in her feet, approached her husband, trembling out of fear of him.

sanskrit: sa tām ṛṣis tataḥ kruddho vākyam āha śubhānanām reṇuke kiṃ cireṇa tvam āgateti punaḥ punaḥ
english: Then the sage, wrathful, spoke these words to the fair-faced woman: "Reṇukā, why have you come so late?"—again and again.

sanskrit: reṇukovāca śiras tāvat pradīptaṃ me pādau caiva tapodhana sūryatejoniruddhāhaṃ vṛkṣacchāyām upāśritā
english: Reṇukā said: My head was aflame, and my feet as well, O treasury of austerity. Held back by the sun's fierce heat, I took refuge in the shade of a tree.

sanskrit: etasmāt kāraṇād brahmaṃś ciram etat kṛtaṃ mayā etaj jñātvā mama vibho mā krudhas tvaṃ tapodhana
english: For this reason, O brāhmaṇa, was this delay caused by me. Knowing this of me, O mighty one, be not wrathful, O treasury of austerity.

sanskrit: jamadagnir uvāca adyainaṃ dīptakiraṇaṃ reṇuke tava duḥkhadam śarair nipātayiṣyāmi sūryam astrāgnitejasā
english: Jamadagni said: This very day, Reṇukā, this sun of blazing rays, the giver of your pain, I shall bring down with my arrows by the fiery power of my weapons.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sa visphārya dhanur divyaṃ gṛhītvā ca bahūñ śarān atiṣṭhat sūryam abhito yato yāti tatomukhaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Drawing taut his celestial bow and taking up many shafts, he stood facing the sun, turning toward whatever quarter it moved.

sanskrit: atha taṃ prahariṣyantaṃ sūryo 'bhyetya vaco 'bravīt dvijarūpeṇa kaunteya kiṃ te sūryo 'parādhyate
english: Then, as he was about to strike, Sūrya, drawing near in the form of a brāhmaṇa, spoke these words, O son of Kuntī: "What wrong has the sun done you?

sanskrit: ādatte raśmibhiḥ sūryo divi vidvaṃs tatas tataḥ rasaṃ sa taṃ vai varṣāsu pravarṣati divākaraḥ
english: With his rays the sun in heaven, O learned one, draws up moisture from here and there; and that essence the day-maker pours down again in the rains.

sanskrit: tato 'nnaṃ jāyate vipra manuṣyāṇāṃ sukhāvaham annaṃ prāṇā iti yathā vedeṣu paripaṭhyate
english: Thence is born food, O brāhmaṇa, that brings well-being to men—for 'food is the breath of life,' as it is recited in the Vedas.

sanskrit: athābhreṣu nigūḍhaś ca raśmibhiḥ parivāritaḥ sapta dvīpān imān brahman varṣeṇābhipravarṣati
english: Then, hidden within the clouds and girt about by his own rays, he rains down with showers upon these seven continents, O brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: tatas tadauṣadhīnāṃ ca vīrudhāṃ patrapuṣpajam sarvaṃ varṣābhinirvṛttam annaṃ saṃbhavati prabho
english: Thence, born of the leaves and flowers of herbs and creepers, all food, brought forth by the rains, comes into being, O lord.

sanskrit: jātakarmāṇi sarvāṇi vratopanayanāni ca godānāni vivāhāś ca tathā yajñasamṛddhayaḥ
english: All the birth-rites, the vows and the initiations, the gifts of cows and the marriages, and likewise the abundance of sacrifices—

sanskrit: satrāṇi dānāni tathā saṃyogā vittasaṃcayāḥ annataḥ saṃpravartante yathā tvaṃ vettha bhārgava
english: the sacrificial sessions and the gifts, the unions and the heapings-up of wealth—all proceed from food, as you well know, O scion of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit: ramaṇīyāni yāvanti yāvad ārambhakāṇi ca sarvam annāt prabhavati viditaṃ kīrtayāmi te
english: Whatever delightful things there are, and whatever undertakings—all arise from food; what is well known I now recount to you.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ hi vettha vipra tvaṃ yad etat kīrtitaṃ mayā prasādaye tvā viprarṣe kiṃ te sūryo nipātyate
english: For all this that I have recounted you yourself know, O brāhmaṇa. I entreat your favor, O brāhmaṇa-sage: why should the sun be struck down by you?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca evaṃ tadā prayācantaṃ bhāskaraṃ munisattamaḥ jamadagnir mahātejāḥ kiṃ kāryaṃ pratyapadyata
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When the light-maker thus pleaded with him, what course did Jamadagni, the best of sages, of great splendor, resolve upon?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tathā prayācamānasya munir agnisamaprabhaḥ jamadagniḥ śamaṃ naiva jagāma kurunandana
english: Bhīṣma said: Though the sun pleaded thus, the sage Jamadagni, radiant as fire, did not come to peace at all, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: tataḥ sūryo madhurayā vācā tam idam abravīt kṛtāñjalir viprarūpī praṇamyedaṃ viśāṃ pate
english: Then Sūrya, in the guise of a brāhmaṇa, with hands joined and bowing low, addressed him in honeyed speech, O lord of peoples:

sanskrit: calaṃ nimittaṃ viprarṣe sadā sūryasya gacchataḥ kathaṃ calaṃ vetsyasi tvaṃ sadā yāntaṃ divākaram
english: "Moving is the mark, O brāhmaṇa-sage, of the ever-traveling sun. How will you take aim at the moving day-maker, who is forever in motion?"

sanskrit: jamadagnir uvāca sthiraṃ vāpi calaṃ vāpi jāne tvāṃ jñānacakṣuṣā avaśyaṃ vinayādhānaṃ kāryam adya mayā tava
english: Jamadagni said: Whether still or moving, I know you with the eye of knowledge. Without fail, today, the imparting of discipline must be wrought upon you by me.

sanskrit: aparāhṇe nimeṣārdhaṃ tiṣṭhasi tvaṃ divākara tatra vetsyāmi sūrya tvāṃ na me 'trāsti vicāraṇā
english: In the afternoon you pause for half the blink of an eye, O day-maker; there I shall mark you, O Sūrya. Of this I have no doubt.

sanskrit: sūrya uvāca asaṃśayaṃ māṃ viprarṣe vetsyase dhanvināṃ vara apakāriṇaṃ tu māṃ viddhi bhagavañ śaraṇāgatam
english: Sūrya said: Without a doubt you will mark me, O brāhmaṇa-sage, O best of bowmen. Yet though I have done you injury, know me, blessed one, as one who has come to you for refuge.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tataḥ prahasya bhagavāñ jamadagnir uvāca tam na bhīḥ sūrya tvayā kāryā praṇipātagato hy asi
english: Bhīṣma said: Then the blessed Jamadagni laughed and said to him: "No fear need be felt by you, O Sūrya, for you have come to me in submission.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇeṣv ārjavaṃ yac ca sthairyaṃ ca dharaṇītale saumyatāṃ caiva somasya gāmbhīryaṃ varuṇasya ca
english: The uprightness that is in brāhmaṇas, and the steadfastness in the surface of the earth, the gentleness of the moon, and the depth of Varuṇa,

sanskrit: dīptim agneḥ prabhāṃ meroḥ pratāpaṃ tapanasya ca etāny atikramed yo vai sa hanyāc charaṇāgatam
english: the blaze of Agni, the radiance of Meru, and the scorching might of the burning sun—whoever would transgress these, he might slay one who has sought refuge.

sanskrit: bhavet sa gurutalpī ca brahmahā ca tathā bhavet surāpānaṃ ca kuryāt sa yo hanyāc charaṇāgatam
english: He who slays one who has sought refuge would be as a defiler of his teacher's bed, and would be as a slayer of a brāhmaṇa, and would be as one who drinks strong liquor.

sanskrit: etasya tv apanītasya samādhiṃ tāta cintaya yathā sukhagamaḥ panthā bhavet tvadraśmitāpitaḥ
english: But, my friend, devise a remedy for this misfortune, so that the path, scorched by your rays, may become easy to travel."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca etāvad uktvā sa tadā tūṣṇīm āsīd bhṛgūdvahaḥ atha sūryo dadau tasmai chatropānaham āśu vai
english: Bhīṣma said: Having said only this much, the upholder of the Bhṛgus then fell silent; whereupon Sūrya at once gave him a parasol and a pair of sandals.

sanskrit: sūrya uvāca maharṣe śirasas trāṇaṃ chatraṃ madraśmivāraṇam pratigṛhṇīṣva padbhyāṃ ca trāṇārthaṃ carmapāduke
english: Sūrya said: O great sage, accept this parasol, a shelter for the head that wards off my rays, and these leather sandals for the protection of the feet.

sanskrit: adyaprabhṛti caivaital loke saṃpracariṣyati puṇyadāneṣu sarveṣu param akṣayyam eva ca
english: And from this day forth this shall pass current in the world, and in all meritorious gifts it shall be supreme and imperishable.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca upānacchatram etad vai sūryeṇeha pravartitam puṇyam etad abhikhyātaṃ triṣu lokeṣu bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus were the sandals and the parasol set in motion here by Sūrya; this meritorious thing is renowned throughout the three worlds, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tasmāt prayaccha viprebhyaś chatropānaham uttamam dharmas te sumahān bhāvī na me 'trāsti vicāraṇā
english: Therefore bestow upon brāhmaṇas the finest parasol and sandals; great indeed shall be your merit. Of this I have no doubt.

sanskrit: chatraṃ hi bharataśreṣṭha yaḥ pradadyād dvijātaye śubhraṃ śataśalākaṃ vai sa pretya sukham edhate
english: For whoever, O best of the Bharatas, should give to a brāhmaṇa a parasol, white and of a hundred ribs, he, when he has departed, flourishes in happiness.

sanskrit: sa śakraloke vasati pūjyamāno dvijātibhiḥ apsarobhiś ca satataṃ devaiś ca bharatarṣabha
english: He dwells in the world of Śakra, ever honored by brāhmaṇas and by the apsarases and by the gods, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: dahyamānāya viprāya yaḥ prayacchaty upānahau snātakāya mahābāho saṃśitāya dvijātaye
english: He who gives a pair of sandals to a brāhmaṇa scorched by the heat, to a snātaka, O mighty-armed one, to a brāhmaṇa firm in his vows—

sanskrit: so 'pi lokān avāpnoti daivatair abhipūjitān goloke sa mudā yukto vasati pretya bhārata
english: he too attains worlds honored by the gods, and in the world of cows, filled with joy, he dwells when he has departed, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: etat te bharataśreṣṭha mayā kārtsnyena kīrtitam chatropānahadānasya phalaṃ bharatasattama
english: This, O best of the Bharatas, has been told by me in full—the fruit of the gift of parasol and sandals, O most excellent of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca supradarśā vanavatī citradhātuvibhūṣitā upetā sarvabījaiś ca śreṣṭhā bhūmir ihocyate
english: Bhīṣma said: Fair to behold, clothed in forest, adorned with bright mineral ores, and furnished with all seeds—such land is here said to be the best.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ kṣetraviśeṣaṃ ca taḍāgānāṃ niveśanam audakāni ca sarvāṇi pravakṣyāmy anupūrvaśaḥ
english: Of its choice tracts, and of the establishing of tanks, and of all matters concerning water, I shall speak in due order.

sanskrit: taḍāgānāṃ ca vakṣyāmi kṛtānāṃ cāpi ye guṇāḥ triṣu lokeṣu sarvatra pūjito yas taḍāgavān
english: I shall tell, too, what virtues belong to tanks once they are made; throughout the three worlds, everywhere honored is he who possesses a tank.

sanskrit: atha vā mitrasadanaṃ maitraṃ mitravivardhanam kīrtisaṃjananaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ taḍāgānāṃ niveśanam
english: The establishing of tanks is a dwelling-place of friends, friendly, an increaser of friends, a begetter of fame, and most excellent.

sanskrit: dharmasyārthasya kāmasya phalam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ taḍāgaṃ sukṛtaṃ deśe kṣetram eva mahāśrayam
english: The wise declare a tank well made in a fitting region to be the fruit of dharma, of artha, and of kāma—a very field that is a great refuge.

sanskrit: caturvidhānāṃ bhūtānāṃ taḍāgam upalakṣayet taḍāgāni ca sarvāṇi diśanti śriyam uttamām
english: One should regard a tank as belonging to creatures of the four kinds, and all tanks bestow the highest prosperity.

sanskrit: devā manuṣyā gandharvāḥ pitaroragarākṣasāḥ sthāvarāṇi ca bhūtāni saṃśrayanti jalāśayam
english: Gods, men, gandharvas, ancestors, serpents and rākṣasas, and the unmoving creatures too, all resort to a reservoir of water.

sanskrit: tasmāt tāṃs te pravakṣyāmi taḍāge ye guṇāḥ smṛtāḥ yā ca tatra phalāvāptir ṛṣibhiḥ samudāhṛtā
english: Therefore I shall declare to you those virtues that are remembered as belonging to a tank, and the winning of fruit therein, as proclaimed by the sages.

sanskrit: varṣamātre taḍāge tu salilaṃ yasya tiṣṭhati agnihotraphalaṃ tasya phalam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: When in a tank the water of a single rainy season abides for a man, the wise declare his fruit to be the fruit of the agnihotra.

sanskrit: śaratkāle tu salilaṃ taḍāge yasya tiṣṭhati gosahasrasya sa pretya labhate phalam uttamam
english: When in his tank the water abides through the autumn season, he, when he has departed, gains the supreme fruit of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: hemantakāle salilaṃ taḍāge yasya tiṣṭhati sa vai bahusuvarṇasya yajñasya labhate phalam
english: When the water abides in his tank through the season of early winter, he gains the fruit of a sacrifice rich in gold.

sanskrit: yasya vai śaiśire kāle taḍāge salilaṃ bhavet agniṣṭomasya yajñasya phalam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: For him in whose tank there is water in the cold season, the wise declare the fruit to be that of the agniṣṭoma sacrifice.

sanskrit: taḍāgaṃ sukṛtaṃ yasya vasante tu mahāśrayam atirātrasya yajñasya phalaṃ sa samupāśnute
english: He whose well-made tank is a great refuge in the spring enjoys the fruit of the atirātra sacrifice.

sanskrit: nidāghakāle pānīyaṃ taḍāge yasya tiṣṭhati vājapeyasamaṃ tasya phalaṃ vai munayo viduḥ
english: When in the hot season the drinking-water abides in his tank, the sages know his fruit to be equal to that of the vājapeya.

sanskrit: sa kulaṃ tārayet sarvaṃ yasya khāte jalāśaye gāvaḥ pibanti pānīyaṃ sādhavaś ca narāḥ sadā
english: He delivers his whole lineage, in whose excavated reservoir cows drink water, and good men always.

sanskrit: taḍāge yasya gāvas tu pibanti tṛṣitā jalam mṛgapakṣimanuṣyāś ca so 'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet
english: He in whose tank thirsting cows drink the water, and deer and birds and men, gains the fruit of the horse-sacrifice.

sanskrit: yat pibanti jalaṃ tatra snāyante viśramanti ca taḍāgadasya tat sarvaṃ pretyānantyāya kalpate
english: Whatever water they drink there, and where they bathe and rest—all this avails the giver of the tank, when he has departed, for eternity.

sanskrit: durlabhaṃ salilaṃ tāta viśeṣeṇa paratra vai pānīyasya pradānena prītir bhavati śāśvatī
english: Water is hard to come by, my friend, and especially so in the world beyond; through the gift of drinking-water, lasting contentment arises.

sanskrit: tilān dadata pānīyaṃ dīpān dadata jāgrata jñātibhiḥ saha modadhvam etat preteṣu durlabham
english: Give sesame, give drinking-water, give lamps, and keep watchful; rejoice together with your kinsmen—for among the departed these things are hard to come by.

sanskrit: sarvadānair gurutaraṃ sarvadānair viśiṣyate pānīyaṃ naraśārdūla tasmād dātavyam eva hi
english: Heavier than all gifts, and distinguished above all gifts, is drinking-water, O tiger among men; therefore it must surely be given.

sanskrit: evam etat taḍāgeṣu kīrtitaṃ phalam uttamam ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi vṛkṣāṇām api ropaṇe
english: Thus has the supreme fruit that lies in tanks been told; hereafter I shall speak of the planting of trees as well.

sanskrit: sthāvarāṇāṃ ca bhūtānāṃ jātayaḥ ṣaṭ prakīrtitāḥ vṛkṣagulmalatāvallyas tvaksārās tṛṇajātayaḥ
english: Of unmoving beings six kinds are proclaimed: trees, shrubs, climbers, creepers, those whose pith lies in the bark, and the grasses.

sanskrit: etā jātyas tu vṛkṣāṇāṃ teṣāṃ rope guṇās tv ime kīrtiś ca mānuṣe loke pretya caiva phalaṃ śubham
english: These are the kinds of trees; in the planting of them these are the virtues—fame in the world of men, and after death a blessed fruit as well.

sanskrit: labhate nāma loke ca pitṛbhiś ca mahīyate devalokagatasyāpi nāma tasya na naśyati
english: He wins renown in the world and is honored by the ancestors; even when he has gone to the world of the gods, his name does not perish.

sanskrit: atītānāgate cobhe pitṛvaṃśaṃ ca bhārata tārayed vṛkṣaropī ca tasmād vṛkṣān praropayet
english: The planter of trees delivers both his line of ancestors, past and yet to come, O Bhārata; therefore let one plant trees.

sanskrit: tasya putrā bhavanty ete pādapā nātra saṃśayaḥ paralokagataḥ svargaṃ lokāṃś cāpnoti so 'vyayān
english: These trees become his sons—of this there is no doubt; and when he has passed to the other world, he attains heaven and imperishable realms.

sanskrit: puṣpaiḥ suragaṇān vṛkṣāḥ phalaiś cāpi tathā pitṝn chāyayā cātithīṃs tāta pūjayanti mahīruhāḥ
english: With their blossoms the trees honor the hosts of the gods, and with their fruits the ancestors, and with their shade the guests, my friend—these earth-born ones.

sanskrit: kiṃnaroragarakṣāṃsi devagandharvamānavāḥ tathā ṛṣigaṇāś caiva saṃśrayanti mahīruhān
english: Kinnaras, serpents, and rākṣasas, gods, gandharvas, and men, and the hosts of sages too, all take refuge in the trees.

sanskrit: puṣpitāḥ phalavantaś ca tarpayantīha mānavān vṛkṣadaṃ putravad vṛkṣās tārayanti paratra ca
english: Blossoming and bearing fruit, they gratify men here; and as sons do, the trees deliver the giver of trees in the world beyond.

sanskrit: tasmāt taḍāge vṛkṣā vai ropyāḥ śreyorthinā sadā putravat paripālyāś ca putrās te dharmataḥ smṛtāḥ
english: Therefore by one who seeks the good, trees should ever be planted beside a tank, and should be tended as one's sons; for in the law they are accounted his sons.

sanskrit: taḍāgakṛd vṛkṣaropī iṣṭayajñaś ca yo dvijaḥ ete svarge mahīyante ye cānye satyavādinaḥ
english: The maker of a tank, the planter of trees, and the brāhmaṇa who has offered sacrifice—these are exalted in heaven, and so are others who speak the truth.
